name: Maximum Reduction
description: Given an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ integers and an integer $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \le k \le n$$$), where each element of the array is denoted by $$$a_i$$$ ($$$0 \le i \lt n$$$). Perform the operation $$$z$$$ given below on $$$a$$$ and print the value of $$$z(a,k)$$$ modulo $$$10^{9}+7$$$. function z(array a, integer k): if length(a) < k: return 0 else: b = empty array ans = 0 for i = 0 .. (length(a) - k): temp = a[i] for j = i .. (i + k - 1): temp = max(temp, a[j]) append temp to the end of b ans = ans + temp return ans + z(b, k)
input_specification: The first line of input contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \le k \le n \le 10^6$$$) — the length of the initial array $$$a$$$ and the parameter $$$k$$$. The second line of input contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{n - 1}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_{i} \le 10^9$$$) — the elements of the array $$$a$$$.
output_specification: Output the only integer, the value of $$$z(a,k)$$$ modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to N using Fermat's Little Theorem (mod 10^9+7 or 998244353). Answer nCr queries in O(1) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1037F — Maximum Reduction [310. Large Factorials and Binomial Coefficients]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Combinatorial selection $\binom{N}{K} = \frac{N!}{K!(N-K)!} \pmod P$ can be evaluated in $O(1)$ by precomputing factorials $fact[i] = fact[i-1] \cdot i \pmod P$ and inverse factorials $invFact[i] = invFact[i+1] \cdot (i+1) \pmod P$ using Fermat's Little Theorem $a^{P-2} \equiv a^{-1} \pmod P$.
